## Description

**What**: Create the bug-classification registry artifact and its audit test.
**Why**: The epic's headline outcome — making the bug-class map auditable, durable, and operationally connected — requires a structured registry as the single source of truth for all other stories in this epic.
**Scope**:
- IN: plugins/dso/docs/bug-classification-registry.md with 27-slug 9-group taxonomy; plugins/dso/scripts/bug-classification-audit.sh; machine-readable slug list export (e.g., bash-sourceable array or JSON sidecar) consumed by stats script and classifier
- OUT: Classification at bug-close time (S2), backfill (S3), retro integration (S4)

## Done Definitions

- When this story is complete, plugins/dso/docs/bug-classification-registry.md exists with 27 slug entries organized into 9 groups (A-I), each entry having: slug (kebab-case), one-sentence classification question, primary defense layer (enum: planning_review, code_review, matrix_ci, coupling_test, concurrency_test, failure_path_test, defense_manifest_test, release_e2e, operational_process, prose_manifest_test), defense_artifact_ref with explicit prefix discriminator (repo:, plugin:, or absolute:), example tickets (>=2 where evidence exists), applies_to_project_classes enum (all or agent_orchestration)
  <- Satisfies: "SC1: Registry artifact at plugins/dso/docs/bug-classification-registry.md containing 27-slug 9-group taxonomy"
- When this story is complete, the registry exports a machine-readable slug list (e.g., a bash-sourceable SLUGS array or JSON sidecar file) that is the single source of truth consumed by bug-classification-stats.sh and the haiku classifier agent — no consumer re-parses the markdown file independently
  <- Satisfies: "SC1: Registry artifact" + risk-register item 4 (single slug-list contract)
- When this story is complete, plugins/dso/scripts/bug-classification-audit.sh parses the registry and asserts: (a) parsed entry count equals declared total (27 at seed time), (b) every entry has all required fields populated, (c) every defense_artifact_ref resolves (file present, named rubric section grep-matched, or test directory present)
  <- Satisfies: "SC2: Audit test parses registry and asserts entry count, required fields, defense_artifact_ref resolution"
- When this story is complete, a mutation test confirms that a deliberately broken defense_artifact_ref causes audit failure with a clear error message identifying the broken slug
  <- Satisfies: "SC2: mutation test confirms detection"
- When this story is complete, the audit test also enumerates all in-use bug-type-* tags across closed tickets and fails (or warns) if any tag references a slug not present in the current registry, or documents the rename procedure for slug migrations
  <- Satisfies: slug-rename safety (adversarial review finding)
- When this story is complete, unit tests are written and passing for all new or modified logic

## Considerations

- [Maintainability] Slug renames must have a coordinated update path: either audit fails if in-use tags reference a non-current slug, OR a tag-migration script is required alongside any future slug rename. Document the chosen approach in the registry header.

## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.
data.title: As a DSO maintainer, I can look up any bug class by slug in a structured registry so that defense artifact references are auditable and machine-verifiable
